findings.description: reports_archive has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor-roster.xlsx seed object it stores) are written without default encryption and rely on unenforced S3 defaults. Sensitive reports data is not encrypted at rest by configuration.
ledger_exports contains no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial ledger exports are stored unencrypted at rest rather than under a KMS or AES256 default.
model_artifacts defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored without configured encryption at rest.
ops_runbooks has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbooks are stored without encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: log bucket policy weakening / missing access logging
findings.description: audit_trail uses the log-delivery-write canned ACL, which grants the S3 log delivery group write access to the bucket. Because this bucket is the logging target for model_artifacts, objects receiving logs from another account's delivery group are writable by that group; combined with the absence of a bucket policy restricting the principal, it weakens the integrity of the audit trail. This is the classic log-bucket target confusion where the target bucket is granted write to the delivery group.
